overview: Finland is a country in northern Europe, between Sweden and Russia. Its capital and largest city is Helsinki. Finland was part of Sweden for centuries and then part of the Russian Empire, before becoming independent in 1917. Finnish and Swedish are both official languages. Finland joined the European Union in 1995 and NATO in 2023.

geography.text: Finland is often called the land of a thousand lakes, but it actually has many tens of thousands. Forests cover around three-quarters of the country. The land is mostly low and gently rolling, shaped by ice sheets during the last Ice Age. The north lies within the Arctic Circle, in Lapland, where the sun does not set for weeks in midsummer.

history.text: For about 600 years Finland was part of the Kingdom of Sweden. In 1809 it became a grand duchy of the Russian Empire, and it declared independence in 1917, during the Russian Revolution. Finland fought the Soviet Union in the Second World War and kept its independence, and later built one of the world's most successful welfare states.

events.title: Russian rule
events.text: Sweden loses Finland to Russia, which makes it a grand duchy.

events.title: Votes for women
events.text: Finland becomes the first country in Europe to give women the vote and the right to stand for parliament.

events.title: Winter War
events.text: Finland fights off a Soviet invasion, though it loses some territory.

events.title: Joins NATO
events.text: Finland becomes a member of NATO.

government.text: Finland is a parliamentary republic. The 200-member parliament, the Eduskunta, chooses the Prime Minister, while the President is elected directly every six years and leads foreign policy together with the government. Finland joined the European Union in 1995 and, after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, NATO in 2023.

economy.text: Finland's economy is built on forests, technology and engineering. Paper, timber and machinery are major exports, and Nokia, once the world's biggest maker of mobile phones, is Finnish. So are the companies behind the games Angry Birds and Clash of Clans.

culture.text: Finland has more saunas than cars, and Finnish sauna culture is on UNESCO's intangible heritage list. Its national epic, the Kalevala, inspired J. R. R. Tolkien. The Moomins, the gentle troll family created by Tove Jansson, are loved worldwide.

items.title: Saunas
items.text: There are around three million saunas in a country of about 5.6 million people.

items.title: Santa Claus Village
items.text: In Rovaniemi on the Arctic Circle in Lapland.

sport.text: Ice hockey is Finland's favourite sport, and it has won the men's world championship four times. Finland has produced many Formula 1 and rally champions, and its runners, such as Paavo Nurmi, dominated distance running in the 1920s.

items.title: Paavo Nurmi
items.text: The 'Flying Finn' won nine Olympic gold medals in the 1920s.

didYouKnow: Finland holds world championships in wife-carrying, air guitar and mobile phone throwing.

keyPeople.name: Jean Sibelius
keyPeople.text: His Finlandia became a symbol of Finnish independence.

keyPeople.name: Linus Torvalds
keyPeople.text: Created Linux, which runs most of the world's servers and every Android phone.
